types.title: Pañcatantra, Hertel's edition (Book I: The Estranging of Friends)
types.description: Sanskrit prose stories with numbered verses quoted by the speakers. Tales are told inside other tales. Prose is set in long paragraphs; a verse is displayed and indented, and the prose after it resumes flush left.

story.description: A story: the frame story of a book, or a tale told inside another story. An inner tale begins with its heading, such as ॥ कथा २१ ॥, and ends with a double danda.

heading.description: A tale heading such as ॥ कथा २१ ॥, or a book title.

paragraph.description: A printed prose paragraph, from an indented line or the start of a tale to the next indented line, heading or tale. A verse quoted by a speaker is inside the paragraph, and the prose after it continues the same paragraph.

lead_in.description: A short line of its own that introduces a quoted verse, such as किं च ।

verse.description: One quoted verse with its number, such as ॥३४८॥.

running_header.description: The running title and the tale title above the rule.

line_number.description: The editor's line numbers in the outer margin (3, 6, 9, …).

margin_mark.description: Any other short mark in the outer margin beside a line.

conventions: Transcribe Devanagari as printed, in Unicode NFC, keeping the edition's word separation, apostrophes and dandas.
